finalText:
It's a small five-file Node app, no framework, no database — just plain `http` and an in-memory `Map` standing in for one.

| File | Job |
|---|---|
| `server.js` | Opens the door. Checks the login token, then hands the request off. |
| `auth.js` | Checks tokens. A user ID plus a signed hash, checked against a secret. |
| `routes.js` | A lookup table: method + path → what to do. |
| `cache.js` | A small memory cache (256 items) that sits in front of reads. |
| `store.js` | The "database." Just a `Map`, records expire in 15 minutes. |

The flow: a request comes into `server.js`, which checks the token with `auth.js` and rejects it if bad. `routes.js` then matches the method and path. Reads (`GET /users`, `GET /orders`) go through `cache.js` first, which falls back to `store.js` on a miss. Writes (`POST /orders`) go straight to `store.js`.

One thing worth knowing before you touch this: the comment in `routes.js` says writes "invalidate the affected keys," but they don't — `putOrder` never clears the cache. So after someone posts a new order, `GET /orders` can keep serving the old list until that cache entry ages out on its own. Worth fixing or at least being aware of.
